note: Semantic verify, 2026-07-29. Judged the winning (cheapest) row of all 492 commodities plus every runner-up within reach of the crown, since a wrong winner is what actually reaches the page. DROP = a different product wearing the commodity's words. NOTE = genuinely the commodity but not strictly like-for-like, so the tile should say so.

entries.reason: Not black pepper. 'Simple Truth Protein Black Pepper Lentils Brown Rice and Ancient Grains Whole Grain Blend' is a seasoned grain side dish; 'black pepper' is a flavour word in its name. It was crowning the spice at $0.34/oz.

Liquid, not ground. 'Stok Cold Brew Coffee Black Unsweetened 48 FL OZ' is ready-to-drink cold brew; comparing its fluid ounces against ground coffee's dry ounces is why it read 66% under the runner-up.

Canned, not fresh. 'Happy Harvest French Green Beans 14.5 OZ' is Aldi's canned-vegetable label; this commodity is fresh green beans priced per pound. It was 49% under the runner-up because a can of beans is not a pound of produce.
Fresh-cut produce, not canned. 'Hy-Vee Short Cuts pineapple chunks' is the refrigerated cut-fruit tub, and the captured line is a fuel-saver ad string quoting $4.99 lb.
Combined A-or-B ad line with a size range: 'Hy-Vee ravioli or tortellini, 42 or 48 oz., $5.99'. Neither which product nor which size is determinable, so the per-ounce price is a coin flip.

Carton beverage, not canned cooking milk. 'Califia Farms Organic Coconut Milk' is the refrigerated drinking carton; this commodity is the thick canned milk used for cooking. Different products, different per-ounce economics.
Not honey. 'Kroger Rich N Honey Hot Dog Buns' is bread that matched on the word honey.
Not fruit. 'Bomb Pop Extremes Super Sour Blue Raspberry Ice Pops' is a freezer novelty that matched on 'raspberry'.
Not fruit. 'Kroger Strawberry Applesauce' matched on 'strawberry' and was crowning fresh berries at $0.083/oz.
Not sesame seeds. 'Ball Park Sesame Seed Burger Buns, 8 Count' is bread.
Not sun-dried tomatoes. 'Mission Sun-Dried Tomato Basil Wraps 6Ct' is flavoured tortillas.
Combined A-or-B-or-C ad line with a size range: 'Pace salsa, picante sauce or queso bowls, 11 to 22 oz., 2/ $5.00'. Two of the three products are not queso and the size spans 2x.
Not pesto. 'Mama Cozzis Pesto Burrata' is a refrigerated pizza/burrata item, and its captured size (1815 OZ) is a mangled decimal we could not prove, so the per-ounce price is unsound as well.

Frozen, not fresh. 'Birds Eye Chopped Spinach' is a freezer box; this commodity is fresh spinach. Frozen spinach is several times denser per ounce, so it undercuts fresh on a per-ounce board without being the same purchase.
Canned, not fresh. 'La Costena Whole Jalapeno Peppers' is the canned pepper; fresh jalapenos are the commodity here and pickled/canned ones already have their own row (pickled-jalapenos).
Cut/canned chunks, not a whole pineapple. This commodity is a whole pineapple priced per each; 'Fareway Chunk Pineapple' is a container of pieces.

Cannot tell fresh from dried. The captured name is just 'Parsley 2 OZ' with no brand - Aldi sells both a Stonemill dried jar and a fresh clamshell in that weight, and at 76% under the runner-up the two readings give very different answers. Dropped rather than publish a guess; dried-parsley still has six other stores.
